theater: 卡累利阿地峽與曼納海姆防線

battle.name: 冬季戰爭
battle.theater: 卡累利阿地峽與曼納海姆防線
battle.brief: 一九三九年十一月三十日蘇聯進攻芬蘭，四〇年三月十三日停火，歷時一百零五天。芬軍在卡累利阿地峽北面的曼納海姆防線死守數月，並以森林中的分割包抄重創蘇軍縱隊。卡面的英國鐵甲艦並未參戰，但「砲塔繞著裝甲轉」的命題，在波羅的海結冰與戰車砲塔被拆作固定碉堡之間，得到一次反面的證明。

kit.name: 鐵甲艦
kit.history: 木殼外面包了鐵。裝甲第一次比砲更難對付，砲塔的設計從此繞著它轉。

countries: 交戰方表面只有兩邊，實際上卻有三股軍隊與一堆旁觀者。芬蘭一邊由國防委員會與參謀總部統率，總統里斯托·呂蒂是政治上的最高權力者，真正握兵權的是受命為芬蘭國防軍總司令的卡爾·古斯塔夫·埃米爾·曼納海姆元帥；前線編制分成三段：地峽軍團由胡戈·厄斯特曼以六個師組成第二軍與第三軍，合計約十二萬人，負責卡累利阿地峽的正面；北方拉普蘭戰區組成特編的拉普蘭兵團，由庫爾特·瓦倫紐斯指揮；拉多加湖以北的戰線由芬軍第四軍與第九師等單位擔任，全軍總人數在三十三萬七千至三十四萬六千五百人之間。芬蘭陣營裡還有外來者：瑞典志願軍全役共八千七百六十人參戰，組成第十九航空團並配備四十公厘波佛斯防空砲營，只在二月底參戰約兩週；法西斯義大利與匈牙利也各派小隊加入，義大利方面甚至把此役視為「反布爾什維克戰爭」。蘇聯一邊由克里姆林宮直接指揮，地面部隊隸屬列寧格勒軍區，先以第十四軍為主、第八軍與第九及第十四狙擊軍為側翼，北方集群的任務是奪取佩察莫的北極港口並推進到羅瓦涅米，同時切斷外國援助芬蘭的通道；海軍方面是波羅的海艦隊，由帕爾迪斯基、塔林與利耶帕亞作基地，負責海上封鎖、掩護兩棲登陸與沿岸轟擊，內務人民委員部的守備部隊則在邊境與要塞先期布防。蘇聯陣營裡還有第三股力量：莫斯科廣播宣佈成立的「芬蘭民主共和國」，由流亡的奧托·威廉莫維奇·庫西寧領導，佔據澤列諾戈爾斯克（特里約基）充當「領土」，手下有一支芬蘭人民軍。國際方面，國際聯盟在十二月十四日將蘇聯除名，美國與瑞典一度嘗試調停均遭拒絕，英法擔心援助芬蘭會把蘇聯推向德國而按兵不動，德國則維持中立但扣留了芬蘭向它與義大利訂購的武器。
countriesEn: On the surface there were only two sides, but in reality there were three armed forces and a crowd of onlookers. On the Finnish side command rested with the Defence Council and the General Staff; President Risto Ryti held the political top position, while actual command of the armed forces went to Field Marshal Carl Gustaf Emil Mannerheim, who was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the Finnish armed forces. The front was divided into three: the Isthmus Corps under Hugo Österman, formed of six divisions grouped into the Second and Third Army, roughly 120,000 men in all, responsible for the Karelian Isthmus; the Lapland theatre in the north, formed into a special Lapland Group under Kurt Wallenius; and the front north of Lake Ladoga, held by the Finnish Fourth Army and the Ninth Division among others. The Finnish camp also contained foreigners: the Swedish Volunteer Corps fielded 8,760 men over the whole war, forming the Nineteenth Flying Regiment and a battery of forty-millimetre Bofors anti-aircraft guns, and fought for roughly two weeks at the end of February; small detachments from Fascist Italy and Hungary joined as well, the Italians regarding the war as a crusade against Bolshevism. On the Soviet side the Kremlin directed everything, the ground forces belonging to the Leningrad Military District, with the Fourteenth Army in front, the Eighth Army and the Ninth and Fourteenth Rifle Corps on the flanks, and the northern group charged with taking the Arctic port of Petsamo, pushing on to Rovaniemi and cutting off the channel of foreign aid to Finland. At sea stood the Baltic Fleet, based at Paldiski, Tallinn and Liepāja, responsible for the maritime blockade, for covering amphibious landings and for coastal gunfire, while NKVD garrison troops took up positions on the frontier and at the fortresses well before the fighting began. There was a third armed force in the Soviet camp: the Finnish Democratic Republic announced over Moscow radio, led by the exiled Otto Villemovich Kuusinen, occupying Zelenogorsk (Terijoki) as its territory, with a Finnish People's Army under it. Internationally, the League of Nations expelled the Soviet Union on 14 December; the United States and Sweden attempted mediation and were refused; Britain and France stood still because they feared that aiding Finland would push the Soviet Union towards Germany, while Germany maintained neutrality but detained the weapons Finland had ordered from it and from Italy.
people: 這場戰爭的勝負其實由少數人的決定造成。芬蘭方面，曼納海姆原本打算辭職——他對政府的樂觀絕望已極，預見局勢惡化得太快才收回辭呈，轉而展開全國動員；他把防衛的骨架放在森林、湖沼、積雪與嚴寒上，堅持分散成小單位、用步槍機槍與反戰車武器去對付裝甲，而不是用血肉去換突破，並在回憶錄裡直截了當拆穿蘇聯關於防線「固若金湯」的說法。總統里斯托·呂蒂在議會裡替軍方擋住割地與驅逐德軍的要求；外長埃利亞斯·埃爾科與國防部長尤霍·紐卡寧為首的強硬派在莫斯科談判中拒絕了全部六項條件，財政部長韋伊諾·坦納與曼納海姆則主張可以接受部分交易，坦納後來在二月中旬飛抵斯德哥爾摩，藉瑞典方面展開談和；代表團則由總統軍事顧問阿拉達爾·帕索寧與駐瑞典大使尤霍·庫斯蒂·巴錫基維率領，巴錫基維被交代絕不可接受在他國領土駐紮蘇軍。前線的名字一個個立起來：亞爾馬·西拉斯沃所率第九師在蘇奧穆斯薩爾米阻止蘇軍第四十四狙擊師增援、於二十五日切斷第一百六十三師的補給線，使該師在十二月二十八日被殲滅、第四十四師在拉泰路隨即被消滅；參謀總長哈拉爾德·厄奎斯特主持全軍冬季作戰條例，狙擊手席摩·海赫在百餘天內擊斃超過五百名蘇軍士兵，芬蘭議會在受攻擊當晚集會，並遷往考哈約基以避空襲。蘇聯那邊，史達林拍板開戰並全程封鎖消息，莫洛托夫在談判與輿論戰中主導一切，庫利克元帥被指親自督導了邁尼拉事件；梅列茨科夫原以「兩週結束」的估計指揮第十四軍卻屢攻不下，十二月二十八日蘇軍在卡累利阿轉入防禦、十二月九日他交出指揮權予最高蘇維埃，之後由伏羅希洛夫、庫茲涅佐夫、史達林與沙波什尼科夫直接統籌；一月起西北方面軍成立，鐵木辛哥出任方面軍司令、日丹諾夫任政委，庫茲涅佐夫與沙波什尼科夫著手檢討戰術與訓練體制，改革因此在冬季真正落地。
peopleEn: The outcome of this war was in truth made by the decisions of a handful of men. On the Finnish side Mannerheim had originally meant to resign — his despair at the government's optimism was extreme, and it was only his forecast that matters would deteriorate so fast that he withdrew the resignation and launched a general mobilisation instead. He set the skeleton of the defence on forest, swamp, deep snow and severe cold, insisting on dispersing into small units and meeting armour with rifles, machine guns and anti-tank weapons rather than trading blood for penetrations, and in his memoirs he bluntly demolished the Soviet claims that the line was impregnable. President Risto Ryti shielded the army in parliament against demands for territory and for the expulsion of the German volunteers; the hard line of foreign minister Eljas Erkko and defence minister Juho Niukangas rejected all six Soviet conditions at the Moscow talks, while finance minister Väinö Tanner and Mannerheim argued for accepting part of the deal — Tanner later flew to Stockholm in mid-February and opened negotiations through the Swedes. The delegation was led by the President's military adviser Aladár Paasonen and by ambassador to Sweden Juho Kusti Paasikivi, who was instructed never to accept foreign basing rights for Soviet troops. Names were made on the battlefield: Hjalmar Siilasvuo's Ninth Division prevented the Soviet 44th Rifle Division from reinforcing the 163rd at Suomussalmi and cut the latter's supply line on the 25th, so that the 163rd was destroyed on 28 December and the 44th went down with part of it on the Raate road; the chief of the general staff Harald Öhquist presided over the winter fighting regulations, and the sniper Simo Häyhä killed more than five hundred Soviet soldiers in a hundred days. The Finnish parliament met on the night the war began and moved to Kokkola to get it out of the air raids. On the Soviet side Stalin decided on war and sealed the story off from the start, Molotov ran both the negotiations and the campaign of propaganda, and Marshal Kulik is held to have personally supervised the Mainila incident. Meretskov commanded the Fourteenth Army on the expectation that the campaign would be over in a fortnight and was repulsed again and again; on 28 December the Soviet troops on the Karelian Isthmus went over to the defensive, and on 9 December Meretskov handed over command to the Stavka, after which Voroshilov, Kuznetsov, Stalin and Shaposhnikov directed the war directly. From January a Northwestern Front was created, with Timoshenko as its commander and Zhdanov as commissar, while Kuznetsov and Shaposhnikov set about reviewing tactics and the training system — and it was this reform that actually took hold during the winter.
kits: 卡面這件一八六二年的英國鐵甲艦並沒有出現在波羅的海，但它確立的命題——裝甲第一次比砲更難對付，砲塔的設計從此繞著它轉——在這場戰爭裡卻以兩種反面的方式重現。一方面是海上：冬季戰爭期間海上行動非常少，波羅的海自十二月末開始結冰，軍艦幾乎無法動彈，到冬季中期只剩破冰船與潛艇能行動，蘇聯波羅的海艦隊本質上是一支近岸防禦型海軍，雖有兩艘戰鬥艦、一艘重巡洋艦、約二十艘驅逐艦、五十艘魚雷艇與五十二艘潛艇，卻缺乏訓練、後勤體制與陸基飛機，難以執行大規模行動；芬蘭海軍同樣是岸防型編制，由兩艘岸防戰艦伊爾瑪利寧號與萬奈摩寧號、五艘潛艇、四艘砲艇、七艘魚雷艇、一艘佈雷艇與六艘佈雷艦組成，兩艘岸防戰艦被轉移到圖爾庫增強當地防空火力。另一方面是陸上：卡面那種「砲位與射界繞著防護核心佈置」的構思，變成了卡累利阿地峽北面的碉堡群與波羅的海沿岸的岸防重砲——芬蘭大部分岸防砲是帝俄統治時期留下的，以一五二公厘口徑者最多，另有新裝的砲塔，最大者達三〇五公厘口徑，原預計與愛沙尼亞合作封鎖蘇聯駛入芬蘭灣的航路；地峽東側的薩科拉、拉多加湖東北岸的曼齊島與地峽西南岸的普里莫爾斯克上的要塞砲，都在初期戰鬥中發揮作用。裝甲這條線上，芬軍的處境更可說是對卡面諷刺的反面：維克斯六噸戰車共採購三十三輛但開戰之初多數不具備武裝，一次大戰遺留的二十輛雷諾 FT-17 戰車則被芬軍認定已經跟不上時代，於是連砲塔都拆下送到曼納海姆防線當作固定碉堡使用，裝甲車的砲塔脫離了底盤，反而變成了不動的砲位。地面火力方面，芬軍主力步槍是沙俄軍火庫遺留的十九萬把莫辛-納甘步槍，另有少量進口日產三八式，與蘇軍步槍同款，可以以戰養戰；火砲主要是俄造七十六公厘野戰砲，另有裝備四千餘把的索米 M1931 衝鋒槍；最缺乏的是反戰車手段，標準武器波佛斯三十七公厘在初期不到一百門，只能以野戰砲、拉赫蒂 L-39 反戰車步槍以及通稱「莫洛托夫雞尾酒」的汽油彈來擊毀戰車。蘇軍一側則以 T-26 縱隊為裝甲主力，全役損失戰車三千五百四十三輛；其砲兵以野戰砲與榴彈砲構成火力底層，二月一日的攻勢光是頭二十四小時的彈幕就傾瀉了三十萬發砲彈；空軍出動約四萬四千架次，損失飛機二百六十一至五百一十五架，芬軍則損失六十二架。
kitsEn: The British ironclad of 1862 on the card never appeared in the Baltic, but the proposition it established — that armour for the first time proved harder to deal with than guns, so that turret design came to revolve around the armour — returns in this war in two inverse forms. First at sea: naval action in the Winter War was very scarce, the Baltic froze from the end of December so that warships could scarcely move, and by the middle of the winter only icebreakers and submarines could operate. The Soviet Baltic Fleet was essentially a coast-defence navy: with two battleships, one heavy cruiser, some twenty destroyers, fifty torpedo boats and fifty-two submarines, it lacked the training, the logistics and the land-based aircraft needed for large-scale operations. The Finnish navy was likewise a coast-defence force, made up of the two coastal defence ships Ilmarinen and Väinämöinen, five submarines, four gunboats, seven torpedo boats, one minelayer and six mine-laying vessels, and the two coastal ships were shifted to Turku to reinforce the air defences there. Second on land: the notion on the card that gun positions and fields of fire are laid out around a protected core became the bunker complexes on the northern side of the Karelian Isthmus and the heavy coastal guns around the Baltic. Most of the Finnish coastal artillery was inherited from the imperial Russian period, the 152-millimetre calibre being the most numerous, alongside newly fitted turrets of up to 305 millimetres, originally intended to operate with Estonia in closing the sea route into the Gulf of Finland; the fortress guns at Sakkola on the eastern isthmus, on Mantsinsaari off the north-east shore of Lake Ladoga and at Primorsk on the south-west shore all contributed in the opening fighting. On the armour question the Finnish case is the exact inverse of the card's irony: of the thirty-three Vickers six-ton tanks purchased, many were unarmed when the war broke out, and the twenty Renault FT-17 tanks left over from the First World War were judged to have fallen behind the times, so that even their turrets were unbolted and sent to the Mannerheim Line to serve as fixed bunkers — the tank turret separated from its chassis and became an immobile gun position. In the way of ground firepower, the Finnish main rifle was 190,000 Mosin-Nagants left over from the Tsarist arsenals, with a small amount of imported Japanese Type 38, same as the Soviet rifle, so ammunition could be taken from the battlefield and used as they fought; the artillery was chiefly the Russian 76-millimetre field gun, and there were more than four thousand Suomi M1931 submachine guns. What they lacked above all was anti-tank power: the standard Bofors 37-millimetre numbered fewer than a hundred at the outset, so field guns, the Lahti L-39 anti-tank rifle and what were known as Molotov cocktails — bottles of fuel — were used to destroy tanks. On the Soviet side columns of T-26s were the armoured main effort and the war cost them 3,543 tanks; their artillery formed the base of firepower, the opening barrage of the 1 February offensive alone pouring three hundred thousand shells in twenty-four hours, while the air force flew some 44,000 sorties and lost 261 to 515 aircraft against the sixty-two the Finns lost.
tactics: 芬軍的戰術核心是「不戰而屈人之兵」的森林消耗：把防禦縱深拉成稀疏的據點網，蘇軍縱隊進入森林後即失去射界與統一指揮，公路上的縱隊被切斷前後，燃料與彈藥在零下三十度以下迅速失效，步兵在雪地裡凍傷、飢餓與耗盡彈藥，最後成建制投降。曼納海姆防線本身是縱深梯次配置，鋼筋混凝土碉堡、土木工事與反戰車壕、機槍巢交錯連接，射擊一律指向可能接近的方向，蘇軍必須逐點攻破，速率極慢。芬軍大量使用冬裝，步兵以散兵依托樹幹射擊，衝鋒槍與輕機槍在近距離橫掃；主動反擊時以滑雪部隊切斷蘇軍側翼公路，再用反戰車步槍逐段殲滅被拖慢的裝甲集群，蘇軍士兵甚至被要求換上白色雪地迷彩裝。蘇軍的戰術則相反：企圖以密集火砲一舉覆蓋防線，再以步兵集團在窄正面強攻，裝甲部隊被當作楔子插入缺口，步兵與車輛跟進突擊——但初期這種打法在卡累利阿幾乎毫無效果，第7軍團把七成半兵力壓在泰帕萊與姆納蘇沼澤之間僅十六公里的窄正面反覆猛攻仍被擋下，一月全月蘇軍沒有真正的大規模進攻，只以轟炸機對防線投下四千八百一十七架次的炸彈。轉折點在二月一日，蘇軍加強砲擊與空中轟炸發動大規模攻勢，頭二十四小時的彈幕就傾瀉了三十萬發砲彈，長時間持續的轟擊一改先前短促射擊的作法，令芬軍在塹壕戰中再折損三千餘人；步兵衝鋒仍以開闊地上的密集隊形進行，但這次投入的戰車較少又有步兵掩護，芬軍無法輕易摧毀。經過連續十天日以繼夜的砲轟，蘇軍終於在地峽西側的蘇馬取得突破，二月十一日在地峽佈署約四十六萬人、超過三千三百五十門火砲、約三千輛戰車與約一千三百架飛機，而與之對陣的只是芬軍八個師共十五萬人，芬軍逐個師後退，二月十五日曼納海姆下令第二軍向中間防線總撤退；地峽東部則仍在抵抗並擊退進攻。
tacticsEn: The core of Finnish tactics was a forest attrition fought without battles: the defence was spread into a sparse net of strongpoints, so that Soviet columns entering the forest lost both field of fire and unified command, while columns on the roads had head and tail cut off and their fuel and ammunition failed quickly at temperatures below minus thirty, leaving infantry to freeze, starve and run out of cartridges before they surrendered in organised groups. The Mannerheim Line itself was laid out in echeloned depth, with reinforced concrete bunkers, earthworks, anti-tank ditches and machine-gun nests interlaced, every gun facing the direction from which an approach might come, so the Soviets had to break the line point by point at a very slow rate of advance. The Finns used winter clothing heavily, and Soviet soldiers were even required to change into white snow camouflage, individual riflemen shooting from tree trunks, submachine guns and light machine guns sweeping the short ranges; in their counteroffensives ski troops cut the roads on the Soviet flanks and anti-tank rifles killed off the armoured groups one segment at a time. Soviet tactics ran the other way: massed artillery was expected to overwhelm the line, infantry groups attacked on a narrow front, and armour was used as a wedge driven into the breach with infantry and vehicles following behind. But in the first phase this approach achieved almost nothing on the Karelian Isthmus: the Seventh Army concentrated seventy-five per cent of its strength on a front only sixteen kilometres wide between Taipale and the Munasuo marshes and was repulsed again and again, and throughout January the Soviets launched no real large-scale offensive, merely flying 4,817 bombing sorties against the line. The turning point came on 1 February, when massed bombardment and air attack opened a general offensive, the barrage of the first twenty-four hours alone pouring three hundred thousand shells, and the long sustained bombardment — a change from the short, sharp bombardments of before — cost the Finns more than three thousand men in the trench fighting. The infantry assault still went in in dense formations across open ground, but this time fewer tanks were committed and they were covered by infantry, so the Finns could not destroy them easily. After ten days and nights of continuous shelling the Soviets finally broke through at Summa on the western side of the isthmus, and on 11 February deployed about 460,000 men, more than 3,350 guns, some 3,000 tanks and about 1,300 aircraft on the isthmus against the eight Finnish divisions and 150,000 men facing them. The Finnish divisions withdrew one by one, and on 15 February Mannerheim ordered the Second Army back in a general retreat to the intermediate line, while in the eastern part of the isthmus the Finns continued to hold and turned attacks back.
data: 戰役自一九三九年十一月三十日至一九四〇年三月十三日，共一百零五天。兵力方面，芬軍投入三十三萬七千至三十四萬六千五百人、戰車三十二輛、飛機一百四十五至二百八十七架；蘇軍在十一月底為四十五萬人，一九四〇年一月一日增至五十五萬零七百五十七人，至三月初達七十六萬零五百七十八人，全役總投入兵力九十八萬八千一百人，戰車二千五百一十四至六千五百四十一輛，飛機三千二百五十三架。戰前一個月列寧格勒軍區僅有二十個師，到戰爭結束前兩週蘇軍已在該軍區投入五十八個師。曼納海姆防線沿地峽修有二百二十一座強化據點，大部分建於一九二〇年代初，其餘為三〇年代後期擴建，實際上多數地段每公里僅有一處鋼筋混凝土碉堡；蘇軍方面則宣稱防線縱深八十至九十公里、有三百五十座鋼筋混凝土工事可承受二百零三毫米砲彈直接命中、另有二千四百座土木工事，蘇聯官方並把它吹成「百萬要塞」，芬蘭史家則指出防線實質上多由壕溝與地下掩體組成。傷亡方面，芬軍陣亡或失蹤二萬五千九百零四人、受傷四萬三千五百五十七人、被俘約一千人，總傷亡約七萬人；蘇軍陣亡或失蹤十二萬六千八百七十五人、受傷十八萬八千六百七十一人、被俘五千五百七十二人、損失戰車三千五百四十三輛、飛機二百六十一至五百一十五架，總傷亡約三十二萬三千人。單場戰鬥的懸殊對比見於拉泰路之戰：蘇軍在此付出七千至九千人的死傷，芬軍只損失四百人。距離與時間上，蘇奧穆斯薩爾米至拉泰路公路段是芬軍分割包抄的重點；防線突破戰自二月一日起至二月十一日，前後約十天；二月十五日芬軍下令總撤退，三月五日蘇軍挺進至防線後方十至十五公里並攻入維堡郊區，同時在維堡灣西側建立灘頭堡，三月七日芬蘭和談代表團抵達莫斯科，三月九日地峽芬軍彈藥告罄、武器消耗殆盡，三月十二日簽約。
dataEn: The campaign ran from 30 November 1939 to 13 March 1940, one hundred and five days in all. On strength: Finland committed between 337,000 and 346,500 men, thirty-two tanks and 145 to 287 aircraft; the Soviet Union had 450,000 men at the end of November, 550,757 on 1 January 1940 and 760,578 by early March, with 998,100 men committed over the war in all, 2,514 to 6,541 tanks and 3,253 aircraft. A month before the war the Leningrad Military District had only twenty divisions; two weeks before it ended the Soviets had committed fifty-eight divisions to that district alone. The Mannerheim Line had 221 reinforced positions built along the isthmus, most of them dating from the early 1920s with many more enlarged in the late 1930s, and in practice most stretches had only one reinforced concrete bunker per kilometre; the Soviet side instead claimed a depth of eighty to ninety kilometres, 350 reinforced concrete works able to take a direct hit from a 203-millimetre shell and a further 2,400 earthworks, and the official line was blown up as the million-fortress. On casualties: the Finns had 25,904 dead or missing, 43,557 wounded and about a thousand taken prisoner, for total losses of some 70,000; the Soviets had 126,875 dead or missing, 188,671 wounded, 5,572 prisoners, 3,543 tanks and 261 to 515 aircraft lost, for total losses of around 323,000. The disproportion of a single engagement shows at the battle of the Raate road, where the Soviets paid 7,000 to 9,000 dead and wounded and the Finns lost four hundred men. On distance and timing: the Suomussalmi-to-Raate road stretch was where the Finnish encirclement was carried out; the breakthrough battle on the line ran from 1 February to about 11 February, roughly ten days; on 15 February the Finns ordered the general retreat, on 5 March the Soviets advanced to within ten to fifteen kilometres behind the line and entered the outskirts of Vyborg while establishing a beachhead on the western side of the Vyborg Bay, on 7 March the Finnish peace delegation arrived in Moscow, on 9 March the Finnish troops on the isthmus had run out of ammunition and worn out their weapons, and the treaty was signed on the 12th.
cause: 開戰的根由是蘇聯對芬蘭邊界安全的不信任，同時混著三十年代談判的死局。一九三九年八月蘇德互不侵犯條約瓜分波羅的海國家勢力範圍，愛沙尼亞、拉脫維亞與立陶宛先後接受蘇聯在境內設基地與駐軍的要求，芬蘭方面的壓力隨即升級：蘇聯要求地峽邊界西推十二公里、租借雷巴奇半島並駐紮五千兵、割讓佩察莫、租借漢科三十年、割讓數座芬蘭灣島嶼、拆除曼納海姆防線，並簽署互助條約，作為交換願割讓雷波拉與波拉耶爾維共五千五百二十九平方公里的未開發林地。芬蘭代表團由總統軍事顧問帕索寧與駐瑞典大使巴錫基維率領，被嚴令不得接受任何租借安排，理由是租借漢科等於讓蘇聯使用一條長達三百二十公里、途經赫爾辛基的鐵路；財政部長坦納與曼納海姆反而主張接受部分條件，最終以外長埃爾科與國防部長紐卡寧為首的強硬派佔上風，談判在十一月十三日再度破裂。十月十二日起芬蘭全國停課、戲院關閉、限制提領超過兩千馬克的現金作戰備，十一月二十六日蘇聯維埃在受攻擊當晚集會，曼納海姆被任命為芬蘭國防軍總司令，國會隨即遷往考哈約基以避空襲；十一月二十六日蘇聯宣稱邊境邁尼拉村遭芬軍砲擊、蘇軍四人死亡九人受傷，莫洛托夫要求芬方道歉並把軍隊後撤二十至二十五公里。後來俄羅斯與芬蘭的史家研究判定此事是蘇聯內務人民委員部人員所為，亦有資料指砲擊由蘇聯元帥庫利克親自督導，目的正是製造開戰藉口並藉此撕毀兩國互不侵犯條約——蘇聯外長莫洛托夫並不承認民主共和國以外的任何芬蘭政府，宣稱與舊芬蘭政府的一切關係已全部解除。十一月三十日凌晨零時十五分，列寧格勒軍區收到國防人民委員部當日清晨發動進攻的命令，戰爭全面爆發。
causeEn: The root of the war was Soviet distrust of Finnish frontier security, tangled up with the dead end of the negotiations of the nineteen-thirties. In August 1939 the Soviet-German non-aggression pact divided the Baltic countries into spheres of influence, and Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania each in turn accepted Soviet bases and troops on their soil, after which the pressure on Finland rose sharply: the Soviet Union demanded that the frontier on the Karelian Isthmus be pushed twelve kilometres west, that the Rybachy Peninsula be leased with five thousand troops stationed on it, that Petsamo be ceded, that Hanko be leased for thirty years, that several Gulf of Finland islands be handed over, that the Mannerheim Line be dismantled and that a mutual assistance treaty be signed, in exchange for which it offered Repola and Porajärvi, 5,529 square kilometres of undeveloped forest. The Finnish delegation was led by the President's military adviser Paasonen and the ambassador to Sweden Paasikivi, and was strictly instructed to accept no lease of any kind, on the ground that leasing Hanko would hand the Soviets the use of a 320-kilometre railway line running past Helsinki; finance minister Tanner and Mannerheim on the contrary argued for accepting part of the terms, but in the end the hard line led by foreign minister Erkko and defence minister Niukangas prevailed and the talks broke down again on 13 November. The immediate spark was a series of moves on 14 and 26 November: the Soviets annulled the non-aggression treaty and recalled the ambassador; from 12 October Finland closed its schools and cinemas and restricted cash withdrawals as a war measure, and on 12 November the parliament moved the capital to Kokkola; on 26 November the Soviet Union claimed that the village of Mainila on the frontier had been shelled by Finnish artillery, with four Soviet dead and nine wounded, and Molotov demanded an apology and a withdrawal of twenty to twenty-five kilometres. Russian and Finnish historians later concluded that the action was carried out by NKVD personnel, and there is evidence that the shelling was personally supervised by the Soviet marshal Kulik, its purpose being to manufacture a pretext for war and thereby tear up the two countries' non-aggression treaty. At ten past midnight on 30 November the Leningrad Military District received the order from the People's Commissariat for Defence to begin the invasion that same morning, and the war was fully under way.
impact: 這場戰爭改寫了北歐的安全版圖。芬蘭割讓芬蘭灣數座島嶼、卡累利阿地峽、拉多加湖畔卡累利阿、薩拉與雷巴奇半島，租借漢科三十年，蘇聯每年為此支付八百萬芬蘭馬克；依條約芬蘭交出約一成一領土與三成資產，曼納海姆防線必須拆除，但國家主權與軍隊完整保留。軍事上，蘇軍雖勝卻付出遠高於預期的代價：四十六萬人對八個師、數千門砲對數百門砲，最後仍然是以傷亡換取突破，戰後芬蘭歷史學家與蘇聯學者伊薩耶夫都指出防線本身遠不如歐洲同類工事堅固，蘇軍最初「發掘出一條突然無法攻破的防線」這套說法，實是為失利尋找藉口。蘇聯在四〇年四月召開最高軍事會議檢討教訓，前線政治委員權力被削減、紀律與制服重新整頓、火焰發射器等冬季裝備引入、大規模培訓滑雪部隊，這批改動在次年莫斯科保衛戰中起了作用。對外，蘇聯此役的表現令德國國防軍陸軍總參謀部更在一九三九年十二月三十一日的檔案裡給出極低評價，助長了希特勒對巴巴羅薩作戰的信心，芬蘭也在次年加入對蘇作戰的行列，最終在一九四四年退出戰爭。芬蘭方面則贏得國際聲望，邱吉爾在四〇年一月二十日的廣播裡直言紅軍的無能已在全世界面前暴露，英法原已計畫以十萬英軍與三萬五千法軍、於三月二十日自挪威與瑞典登陸支援芬蘭，卻因兩國先後拒絕借道而落空，法國總理達拉第的內閣隨即垮台，盟國的國際威信重挫。
impactEn: The war redrew the security map of northern Europe. Finland ceded several islands in the Gulf of Finland, the Karelian Isthmus, Ladoga Karelia, Salla and the Rybachy Peninsula, and leased Hanko for thirty years, the Soviets paying eight million Finnish marks a year for it; under the treaty Finland gave up about eleven per cent of its territory and thirty per cent of its assets and had to dismantle the Mannerheim Line, but kept its sovereignty and its army intact. Militarily the Soviet Union won, but at a cost far above expectation: 460,000 men against eight divisions, thousands of guns against hundreds, and the breakthrough was in the end bought with blood. After the war Finnish historians and the Soviet scholar Isaev both concluded that the line itself was far weaker than comparable works in Europe, and the Soviet claim that it had suddenly discovered a line which could not be assaulted in haste was in truth an excuse for the failure. In April 1940 the Soviet Union held a high-level military conference to review the lessons: the power of front-line political commissars was curtailed, discipline and uniforms were overhauled, flamethrowers and other winter equipment were introduced, and ski troops were trained on a large scale — changes that were to matter the following year in the defence of Moscow. Abroad, the Soviet performance in this war drew a very low assessment from the German general staff in a document written while it was still being fought, and it strengthened Hitler's confidence in Operation Barbarossa; Finland joined the war against the Soviet Union the following year and eventually withdrew in 1944. On the Finnish side the country gained international standing, Churchill declared in a broadcast on 20 January 1940 that the incompetence of the Red Army had been laid bare before the whole world, and the Anglo-French plan to land in Scandinavia in aid of Finland — a hundred thousand British and thirty-five thousand French troops to land on 20 March — collapsed after Norway and Sweden refused passage in turn, bringing down the Daladier cabinet and badly shaking the Allies' prestige.
result: 結果是蘇聯慘勝：它拿到了地峽與薩拉，芬蘭保住了國家與軍隊。一月全月蘇軍沒有發動真正的大規模進攻，只以第7、第8、第13軍團與空軍持續砲轟與偵查，二月一日才以加倍的砲火與空襲掀起攻勢，頭二十四小時傾瀉三十萬發砲彈，十天連續砲擊後在地峽西側的蘇馬取得突破，二月十一日以約四十六萬人、逾三千三百五十門火砲、約三千輛戰車與約一千三百架飛機壓上，芬軍八個師十五萬人逐個後退，二月十五日曼納海姆下令第二軍總退到中間防線，地峽東部仍在抵抗。戰局一面倒之後，芬蘭外長坦納在二月中旬飛抵斯德哥爾摩借瑞典方面談和；芬蘭政府對蘇聯的嚴苛條件一度猶豫，二月十九日瑞典國王古斯塔夫五世公開宣佈瑞典不再給予芬蘭任何援助；蘇聯代表於二月二十五日交付和約詳細內容，芬方二十九日表示原則上同意參加談判。三月五日蘇軍再挺進至防線後方十至十五公里並攻入維堡郊區、在維堡灣西側建立灘頭堡，芬軍當天提出停戰而蘇方隔天拒絕；三月七日和談代表團抵達莫斯科，蘇方趁形勢有利再提更苛條件，三月九日地峽芬軍彈藥告罄、武器消耗殆盡，而英法遠征又因挪威與瑞典不放行而無望，芬蘭政府最終接受條款，三月十二日在莫斯科簽訂和約，三月十三日於列寧格勒正午時間、赫爾辛基上午十一點停火。和約內容是割讓上述領土、租借漢科並拆除曼納海姆防線，芬蘭則以割地和屈辱換取國家存續；此役留下的「冬季戰爭精神」成為芬蘭民族敘事的核心，也直接推動了芬蘭在一九四一年的再度參戰。
resultEn: The result was a Pyrrhic victory for the Soviet Union: it took the isthmus and Salla, while Finland kept the country and its army. Throughout January the Soviets launched no genuine large-scale offensive, merely keeping up shelling and reconnaissance with the Seventh, Eighth and Thirteenth Armies and the air force; only on 1 February, with doubled artillery and air attack, did the general offensive open, three hundred thousand shells falling in the first twenty-four hours, and after ten days of continuous bombardment the breakthrough came at Summa on the western side of the isthmus. On 11 February some 460,000 men, more than 3,350 guns, some 3,000 tanks and about 1,300 aircraft went forward against eight Finnish divisions and 150,000 men, the Finnish units withdrawing one by one, and on 15 February Mannerheim ordered the Second Army back to the intermediate line, while the eastern part of the isthmus held out. Once the course of the war was settled, foreign minister Tanner flew to Stockholm in mid-February and opened negotiations through the Swedes; the Finnish government hesitated over the harsh Soviet terms, and on 19 February King Gustav V of Sweden announced publicly that Sweden would give Finland no further aid; the Soviet delegation delivered the detailed terms of the peace on 25 February, and on the 29th Finland agreed in principle to take part in talks. On 5 March the Soviets advanced again to within ten to fifteen kilometres behind the line and into the outskirts of Vyborg, establishing a beachhead on the western shore of the Vyborg Bay; the Finns proposed a ceasefire that day and were refused the next; on 7 March the peace delegation reached Moscow, where the Soviets, in a strong position, put forward yet harsher terms, and on the 9th the Finnish troops on the isthmus had run out of ammunition and worn out their weapons, while the Anglo-French expedition was in any case hopeless now that Norway and Sweden would not give passage. Finland accepted the terms, the treaty was signed in Moscow on 12 March, and the ceasefire took effect at noon Leningrad time, eleven in the morning Helsinki time, on the 13th. Its terms were the cession of the territories named, the lease of Hanko and the dismantling of the Mannerheim Line, with Finland buying the survival of the state at the price of territory and humiliation; the Winter War spirit that came out of it became the core of the Finnish national narrative, and it drove Finland directly into taking part in the war again in 1941.
